reviews.text:

Be especially careful with the auto-renew subscription. If you don't cancel it in time, you'll continue to be charged.

In my experience, the stock guidance wasn't worth the subscription price, and much of the content was simply news or financial news that's widely available from other sources. I didn't feel I received enough value to justify the cost.

If you're considering paying for this app, do your research first. Personally, I would have been better off investing the subscription money directly than paying for information I found to be of little value.

reviews.title: 52 Week High Low limit disappeared
reviews.text:
It appears that the entire section displaying 52-week high/low ranges as well as 10-year high/low data has been removed. This information was previously easy to access and extremely valuable for tracking market performance, historical context, and long-term trends.

The removal of this data is quite inconvenient, especially for active investors and long-term market participants who rely on these benchmarks for quick analysis and decision-making. The 52-week and 10-year high/low ranges provide immediate perspective on where a stock stands relative to its historical performance—something that cannot be easily replaced by charts alone.

I’m curious as to why this section was removed, as it was a core feature that differentiated the CNBC app as a practical, investor-friendly tool. Its absence reduces transparency and adds unnecessary friction for users who now need to seek this information elsewhere.

Sadly this feature was taken away, and now I, along with many others no doubt, have to jump over to other financial apps ( or switch over) in order to have this important data.
